q: 61. The resistance of an aggregate to compressive force is known as
explain: The aggregate crushing value test measures the resistance of aggregate to gradually applied compressive (crushing) load.

q: 62. The resistance of an aggregate to the effect of hydration of cement and weather is called
explain: Soundness refers to the ability of aggregate to resist volume changes caused by weathering action, temperature and moisture changes, and chemical reactions such as cement hydration.

q: 63. The resistance of an aggregate to wear is known as
explain: The abrasion value test (e.g., Los Angeles test) measures an aggregate's resistance to wear caused by rubbing/attrition.

q: 64. Bulking of sand is
options: increase in volume of sand due to presence of moisture upto certain extent
explain: Bulking is the apparent increase in volume of a given mass of sand caused by moisture films separating the particles, up to a certain moisture content.

q: 65. With the moisture content of 5 to 10% by weight, the bulking of sand is increased by
explain: At moisture contents in the 5-10% range, sand bulking reaches values on the order of 50% increase in volume as per standard bulking curves.

q: 66. The strength of concrete after one year as compared to 28 days strength is about
explain: Continued hydration over time increases strength beyond the 28-day value; typical long-term gain at one year is about 20-25% more than the 28-day strength.

q: 67. As compared to ordinary Portland cement, high alumina cement has
options: higher initial setting time but lower final setting time
lower initial setting time but higher final setting time
higher initial setting time and final setting time
lower initial setting time and final setting time
explain: High alumina cement is characterized by a longer initial setting time but a comparatively shorter final setting time than OPC, giving rapid strength gain once setting begins.

q: 68. Modulus of rupture of concrete is a measure of
explain: Modulus of rupture is obtained from a flexure (bending) test on a concrete beam and represents its flexural tensile strength.

q: 69. In order to obtain the best workability of concrete, the preferred shape of aggregate is
explain: Rounded aggregate has minimum surface area and least interlocking/friction, which gives the best workability for a given water-cement ratio.

q: 70. Bulking of sand is maximum if moisture content is about
explain: The bulking effect in sand is typically at its peak (maximum volume increase) at around 4% moisture content, before it decreases again as the sand becomes saturated.

q: 71. Finer grinding of cement
options: affects only the early development of strength
explain: Finer grinding increases the surface area available for hydration, which speeds up early reaction and improves early strength development, without significantly changing the ultimate (long-term) strength.

q: 72. Poisons ratio for concrete
explain: As per this text, Poisson's ratio of concrete tends to increase as the mix becomes richer (higher cement content).

q: 73. 1% of voids in concrete mix would reduce its strength by about
explain: As a general rule of thumb used in concrete technology, each 1% of entrapped air voids reduces compressive strength by approximately 5%.

q: 74. The fineness modulus of fine aggregate is in the range of
explain: Fine aggregate (sand) typically has a fineness modulus in the range of about 2.0 to 3.5, differentiating it from coarse aggregate which has a much higher FM.

q: 75. Minimum grade of concrete to be used in RCC as per IS 456: 1978 is
explain: As per the (older) IS 456:1978 provisions referenced here, M10 was permitted as the minimum grade usable in reinforced cement concrete.

q: 76. For concreting of heavily reinforced sections without vibration, the workability of concrete expressed as compacting factor should be
explain: Heavily reinforced sections placed without mechanical vibration need a very high workability mix; the compacting factor required in such cases is above 0.92.

q: 77. Minimum quantity of water needed per 50 kg of cement for M15 grade of concrete is
explain: As per the mix design water requirement tables referenced in this text, M15 grade concrete needs a minimum of about 32 litres of water per 50 kg bag of cement.

q: 78. In case of hand mixing of concrete, the extra cement to be added is
explain: Since hand mixing is less efficient/thorough than machine mixing, an additional 10% cement is recommended to compensate for the loss in mixing efficiency.

q: 79. For walls, columns and vertical faces of all structural members, the formwork is generally removed after
explain: Vertical formwork on walls, columns, and similar faces that carry no load can typically be removed relatively early, within about 24 to 48 hours, since these surfaces are non-load-bearing during curing.

q: 80. The individual variation between test strength of sample should not be more than
explain: As per the code check on scatter of test results, the maximum permitted variation of an individual sample strength from the average is ±5% of the average value.

q: 81. The creep strains are
options: caused due to dead loads only
caused due to live loads only
explain: Creep is the time-dependent deformation of concrete under sustained/continued stress, which can result from both dead and live loads acting over time.

q: 82. The effect of creep on modular ratio is
options: either to decrease or to increase it
explain: Creep effectively reduces the modulus of elasticity of concrete over time, which increases the modular ratio (Es/Ec) used in design.

q: 83. The purpose of reinforcement in pre stress concrete is
options: to impart initial compressive stress in concrete
explain: In prestressed concrete, the tendons/reinforcement are stressed and anchored specifically to impart an initial compressive stress into the concrete before service loads are applied.

q: 84. Which of the following cement is expected to have the highest compressive strength after 3 days
explain: High alumina cement gains strength extremely rapidly, reaching very high compressive strength values within just 1-3 days, higher than the other cement types listed.

q: 85. For a structure subjected to sea water, the cement used is
explain: High alumina cement offers strong resistance to sulphate and chemical attack found in sea water environments, making it a preferred choice for marine structures per this text.

q: 86. The strength of concrete using air entraining cement gets reduced by
explain: Entrained air, while improving workability and frost resistance, reduces the compressive strength of concrete typically by about 10-15%.

q: 87. The ratio of various ingredients in concrete of grade M20 is
explain: M20 grade concrete corresponds to the nominal mix proportion of 1:1.5:3 (cement:fine aggregate:coarse aggregate) as per traditional nominal mix classification.

q: 88. Ware house pack of cement means
options: pressure exertion of the bags of upper layers
pressure compaction of bag on lower layer
explain: Warehouse pack refers to the compaction/hardening effect on lower cement bags caused by the pressure of bags stacked above them during storage.

q: 89. If the effective plan area of ware house is 54 sq. m and maximum height of piles permitted is 270 cm, the number of cement bags to be stored is
explain: Using the standard storage formula (volume ÷ volume per bag) for an area of 54 m² and pile height of 2.7 m, the capacity works out to approximately 2700 bags.

q: 90. The internal dimensions of a warehouse are 15 m × 5.6 m and the maximum height of piles permitted is 270 cm, the maximum number of cement bags to be stored is
explain: For a plan area of 15 × 5.6 = 84 m² and a permitted pile height of 2.7 m, applying the standard storage capacity formula gives approximately 3000 bags.

q: 91. The process of proper and accurate measurement of concrete ingredients for uniformity of proportion is known as
explain: Batching is the operation of accurately measuring out the quantities of cement, aggregates and water for each concrete mix to maintain uniform proportions.

q: 92. High increase in temperature ......... the strength of concrete.
explain: Excessively high curing/placing temperatures accelerate early hydration but result in a weaker, more porous microstructure, ultimately decreasing long-term concrete strength.

q: 93. The concrete mix which is not amicable for smooth finish is said to posses
explain: A harsh concrete mix — one with excessive hardness/harshness due to insufficient fines or paste — is difficult to finish smoothly.

q: 94. The mix proportions of cement mortar to be placed in the joints in precast pre stressed member is
explain: As specified in this text, the cement mortar used for filling joints between precast prestressed members is proportioned at 1:1.5 (cement:sand).

q: 95. The ratio of volume of moist sand to the volume of dry sand is known as
explain: The bulking factor is defined as the ratio of the volume of moist (bulked) sand to the volume of the same mass of dry sand.

q: 96. The fineness modulus of an aggregate is roughly proportional to
options: average size of the particles in the aggregate
explain: Fineness modulus is an empirical index that correlates roughly with the average particle size of the aggregate — a higher FM indicates coarser average particle size.

q: 97. The value of fineness modulus for fine sand may range between
explain: Per the classification used in this text, fine sand typically has a fineness modulus in the range of 2.2 to 2.6.

q: 98. Reduction in the quantity of mixing water which is possibly by the use of plasticizers and admixtures varies from
explain: Ordinary plasticizing admixtures typically allow a water reduction of about 5% to 15% while maintaining the same workability.

q: 99. In concrete mix design, allowance for bulking of sand is necessary in case of
explain: Bulking changes the apparent volume of sand due to moisture, so a correction is required only when proportioning is done by volume (volume batching), not by weight.

q: 100. In concrete mix design, allowance for surface water carried by aggregate is necessary in case of
explain: Surface moisture on aggregate adds extra water to the mix and affects the effective water-cement ratio regardless of whether batching is done by volume or by weight, so an allowance is needed in both cases.

q: 101. Which of the following types of concrete mixers is most commonly used in precast concrete factories?
explain: Pan type mixers, which provide intensive and uniform mixing suited to stiff/low-slump mixes, are most commonly used in precast concrete factory production.

q: 102. Steam curing is not recommended for the concrete using
explain: High alumina cement is highly sensitive to elevated curing temperatures, which can cause conversion reactions that seriously reduce its strength, so steam curing is not recommended for it.

q: 103. Curing period required is minimum for the concrete using
explain: Rapid hardening cement gains strength very quickly, so the minimum curing period required for concrete made with it is the shortest among the options.

q: 104. The cement concrete, from which entrained air and excess water are removed after placing it in position is called
explain: Vacuum concrete is a special process where a vacuum is applied after placing to remove entrapped air and excess water, improving density and strength.

q: 105. The removal of excess air after placing concrete helps in increasing the strength of concrete by
explain: As given in this text, removing excess entrapped air (vacuum dewatering process) improves the strength of concrete by about 15 to 20%.

q: 106. The cement concrete prepared by mixing aluminium in it, is called
explain: Mixing aluminium powder with cement paste generates hydrogen gas bubbles, producing a cellular/aerated, air-entrained lightweight concrete — hence all these terms describe the same product.

q: 107. The light weight concrete is prepared by
options: mixing portland cement with sawdust in specified proportion in the concrete
using coke breeze, cinder or slag as aggregate in the concrete
explain: Light weight concrete is commonly produced by replacing normal aggregate with lightweight materials such as coke breeze, cinder, or slag.

q: 108. The sound absorption coefficient of light weight concrete is nearly ......... than that of ordinary concrete.
explain: Due to its porous structure, light weight concrete has a sound absorption coefficient roughly twice that of ordinary dense concrete.

q: 109. The compressive strength of concrete determined from 150 mm × 150 mm cylinder as compared to that determined from 150 mm cube is
explain: Cylinder specimens generally record lower compressive strength than cube specimens of comparable size due to differences in the stress distribution and end-restraint effects during testing.

q: 110. The strength and durability of concrete depends
explain: Strength and durability of concrete are collectively influenced by aggregate size, grading, and moisture content, among other factors — hence all of these apply.

q: 111. The breaking up of cohesion in a mass of concrete is called
explain: Segregation is defined as the separation/breaking up of the constituent materials of concrete, i.e., loss of cohesion in the fresh mix.

q: 112. The continuous strain which the concrete undergo due to application external loadsis called
explain: Creep is defined as the gradual, time-dependent increase in strain in concrete under sustained (constant) external load.

q: 113. Segregation in concrete results in
explain: Segregation of concrete leads to a range of defects including honeycombing, porous layers, and surface scaling — so all of these are consequences.

q: 114. Harshness in concrete is due to the excess of
explain: Harshness (difficulty in placing/finishing) in a concrete mix occurs when there is a deficiency of fines and an excess of coarser particles relative to the mix design.

q: 115. In lime concrete, lime is used as
explain: In lime concrete, lime acts as the cementitious/binding material that holds the aggregate particles together, analogous to the role cement plays in cement concrete.

q: 116. The type of lime used in lime concrete is
explain: Hydraulic lime, which can set and harden even under water/moist conditions due to its silica and alumina content, is the type generally used in lime concrete construction.

q: 117. The lime concrete has ......... strength as compared to cement concrete.
explain: Lime concrete develops significantly lower strength than cement concrete because lime is a weaker binder than Portland cement.

q: 118. Ferro concrete is another name given to
explain: 'Ferro-concrete' (from the French/Italian term for iron) is another name commonly used for reinforced cement concrete, where steel reinforcement is embedded in concrete.

q: 119. Plain cement concrete is strong in taking
explain: Plain (unreinforced) cement concrete is inherently strong in resisting compressive stresses but weak in tension, which is why steel reinforcement is added for tensile resistance.

q: 120. The cement concrete in which high compressive stresses are artificially induced before its actual use is called
explain: Prestressed concrete is specifically defined as concrete in which internal compressive stresses are deliberately induced before service loading, to counteract anticipated tensile stresses.
